scope: Proposition 6.6 (The countable compatible construction) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: All labels can be processed successively. At every finite stage the packet diagram has the invariant above and no nonempty packet of dimension at most one. After the radial stage it has finite exceptional data on whole packets; at stage zero this assertion holds on buffered compact radial blocks. Its finite reconstruction Xr has a proper collapse qr : Xr → M and closed signed sides P (r) i , N (r) i for each processed center label, with P (r) i ∪ N (r) i = Xr, P (r) i ∩ N (r) i = W (r) i , where W (r) i is its wall. The forced preimages satisfy q−1 r (Ai) ⊂ P (r) i \ W (r) i , q−1 r (Bi) ⊂ N (r) i \ W (r) i . These inclusions hold in open phases and persist at every subsequent finite stage. No n − 1 distinct walls, even including the radial wall, have a common point. Each center wall lies over its original open outer ball, and its components are compact and locally finite. Old horizons can be enlarged by identifications preserving collapse, all walls, and all signed statuses. For any prescribed sequence εr > 0 with P r εr < 1, the next finite collar compression can be chosen with collapse displacement less than εr, preserving the previously decided wall strata and signed sides. These are finite-stage conclusions; the limiting fixed-copy construction is made in the next section.
